blocks.text: Sparse, intimate opening. Solo female voice, close and low, almost spoken. Single accordion breathing underneath

The music stopped before you noticed
And the lights came up like a secret told too soon
Look at you
Hands in your lap like tools between jobs
Still warm from whatever you were feeling
But with nowhere left to put it
Tender observation, same intimacy, voice gaining warmth

The woman to your left was crying
Now she's studying her ring finger
The man behind you cleared his throat
Like an apology for being human
And the dust keeps floating through the spotlight
Doesn't know the show is over
Bowed upright bass enters, simple accordion figure

Palms up is a question
Palms down is a decision
Which are yours right now
Which are yours
Lullaby tempo, maternal, singing to each person individually

Oh sit with it, darlings
Sit with the sawdust and the silence
The duct tape is showing
And so are you
And so are you
Tambourine enters tentatively, clarinet holds a single note

Someone's fingers find a rhythm on their knee
Not performing, just remembering
And the woman with the ring
Looks up and catches someone looking back
And neither one looks away
And that's the whole sermon right there
Building warmth, hand percussion, ensemble creeping in

Oh stay with it, darlings
Stay with the stranger and the stillness
Your hands remember something
Your hands remember
Everything strips back. Just her voice. Space. Tension building through repetition

You came in alone
You sat in the dark alone
You felt it alone
But the lights
The lights
The lights
Full ensemble crashes in — drums, accordion, bass, clarinet, brass. Tempo lifts. Revelry. She's no longer holding the room, the room is carrying her

Oh THERE you are, darlings
There you are with your dust and your thunder
The tent doesn't need a performer
When the audience is the act
Clap those beautiful hands
Clap those beautiful useless holy hands

notebook.style: Junkyard cabaret ballad, female vocalist with warm maternal alto, intimate torch song building to full ensemble revelry, Opens sparse and close — solo voice nearly spoken over a single breathing accordion, like a woman singing in a tent made of salvage and string lights, Bowed upright bass and simple accordion figure enter gradually, Lullaby tempo through first half, tender and unhurried, the sound of a room held carefully, Tambourine and hand percussion creep in midway, tentative, human, like fingers tapping a knee, Clarinet enters on held notes, Bridge strips everything back to solo voice, tension building through repetition and space, Final section erupts — full ramshackle ensemble with drums, accordion, upright bass, clarinet, violin, brass, Tempo lifts into communal celebration, a crowd finding its own rhythm, The arc is a slingshot: pulled back through stillness and vulnerability, released into joyful noise, Warm analog tone, nothing polished, everything held together with duct tape
